advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether pre-release versions (e.g. 0.3.2rc1) should be rejected by require_s3_helper()'s version floor rather than passing via leading-digit parsing.
evidence: src/rebar/_optional.py:138: `for part in parts[:3]:  # Take first 3 components`
src/rebar/_optional.py:141: extracts leading digits then breaks on first non-digit, so '2rc1' -> 2
The guard is meant to fail closed on versions that don't carry the IfNoneMatch lock; a pre-release of the minimum could lack it yet pass
advisory.finding: The stdlib version parser extracts only the leading run of digits per component, so a PEP 440 pre-release like '0.3.2rc1' parses to (0,3,2) and passes the floor, even though a pre-release precedes the final 0.3.2 release; similarly '0.4.0a1' would pass. This is a fail-open corner for pre-release versions.
scenarios: An operator has a pre-release of git-remote-s3 (e.g. 0.3.2rc1) installed without the finalized IfNoneMatch lock behavior

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider an upper bound (e.g. >=0.3.2,<1) on git-remote-s3 to guard against breaking majors, or document why an open upper range is acceptable.
evidence: # helper (Apache-2.0) so `sync.remote` can point at an s3://bucket/prefix remote.
ABSENCE: no license-check config or allowlist entry accompanies the new dependency in the diff
advisory.finding: The new optional dependency git-remote-s3 is pinned with only a lower bound (>=0.3.2) and no upper bound, so a future breaking major release (e.g. 1.0) would satisfy the [s3] extra while the runtime guard require_s3_helper() only enforces the same floor, offering no protection against an incompatible newer major.
merged_from: The pyproject comment asserts git-remote-s3 is Apache-2.0 licensed, but this license posture is not verified or recorded anywhere machine-checkable (no license allowlist entry, no provenance note beyond a code comment).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test covering a version with fewer than 3 components (e.g. '1' succeeds, '0.3' fails as (0,3,0)<(0,3,2)) to exercise the padding branch.
evidence: Test versions used: '0.3.2', '0.2.9', '0.4.0', '0.3.2.post1', 'unknown' — all have >=3 dotted numeric components; none exercises the padding path
ABSENCE: no test asserts a two- or one-component version (e.g. '0.4' or '1') succeeds/fails via the pad-to-3 logic
advisory.finding: The version-padding branch (fewer than 3 dotted components) in require_s3_helper is untested. No test supplies a version like '1' or '0.3' that drives the `while len(parsed_version) < 3: pad with zeros` loop; a regression breaking the padding (e.g. rejecting a valid short version, or index error) would not be caught.
scenarios: An upstream release tagged with a two-component version string reaching the guard
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_edge_short_version` cases: version='1' -> success (pads to (1,0,0)); version='0.3' -> raises (pads to (0,3,0) < (0,3,2)).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a boundary test asserting version='0.3.1' raises OptionalDependencyError (patch just below the 0.3.2 floor).
evidence: ABSENCE: no test asserts '0.3.1' (patch just below floor) is rejected
advisory.finding: The tight patch-level rejection boundary '0.3.1' (one patch below the (0,3,2) minimum, same major.minor) is untested. The only too-old case is '0.2.9', which differs at the minor level, so a regression comparing only major.minor components would still pass all tests while wrongly accepting 0.3.1.
scenarios: An installed git-remote-s3 at 0.3.1 lacking the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock the >=0.3.2 floor guards against
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_edge_patch_just_below_min`: _install(..., version='0.3.1'); assert raises OptionalDependencyError and '0.3.2' in message.
